gloss: ground-breaking ceremony; Shinto rite before construction

definitions.gloss: ground-breaking ceremony; Shinto rite before construction
definitions.explanation: A Shinto ceremony held on a building site before construction starts, to calm the deity of the land and pray for safety during the work. A priest purifies the site, and the owner and builder turn the first earth with a wooden hoe.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}、{地鎮祭|じちんさい}を{行|おこな}います。
examples.english: We will hold the ground-breaking ceremony next week.

examples.japanese: {地鎮祭|じちんさい}には{神主|かんぬし}さんに{来|き}てもらった。
examples.english: We had a Shinto priest come for the ground-breaking ceremony.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}の{安全|あんぜん}を{祈|いの}って、{施主|せしゅ}と{工務店|こうむてん}の{担当者|たんとうしゃ}が{地鎮祭|じちんさい}に{出席|しゅっせき}した。
examples.english: Praying for safety during construction, the client and the builder's representative attended the ground-breaking ceremony.

notes:
{地|じ} (land) + {鎮|ちん} (to calm) + {祭|さい} (rite): a rite to calm the land.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {地鎮祭|じちんさい}を{行|おこな}う: to hold a ground-breaking ceremony
- {地鎮祭|じちんさい}に{出席|しゅっせき}する: to attend the ceremony
- {地鎮祭|じちんさい}の{準備|じゅんび}: preparations for the ceremony

CULTURAL NOTE:
Still routine when a house or public building goes up, even for people who are not otherwise religious; skipping it is a conscious decision. The parallel rite held when the frame is raised is {上棟式|じょうとうしき}, and the one on completion is {竣工式|しゅんこうしき}.
